e-6559.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
e-6559.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 5-9\text{i} \\ -7+8\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-2+5\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{5-9\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-7+8\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2-5\text{i} \\ 5+9\text{i} \\ -7-8\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-6560.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Vector
e-6560.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/19d1bb5ad60407748a9c624dee20931c3c70a4bbc3727c4172cfb40384ab6a72.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/f7539ad7301462681681e738b905633b7aa73ca65b5512063e32fa22bcdc0d09.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/a7976c73a0aeb9f286a281c193b3a00b38e8bc0fa36a30e985fe1e8f80d7796b.png) what is the value of $ab+cd?$
e-6560.worked_solution:
For the given vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/4d6fc79d41790b29a966f7a3303329ab1b778856991ad5b3b85ee3965fce2e33.png) we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $a=-3, b=5, c=7$ and $d=-2,$ which implies that

$$
ab+cd=(-3) \cdot 5 + 7 \cdot (-2) = -29.
$$

e-7345.knowledge_point: Finding the Real or Imaginary Part of a Scalar Given the Conjugate of a Scaled Vector
e-7345.worked_solution:
Since $\overline{k\mathbf{v}} = \overline{k} \, \overline{\mathbf{v}},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i}\,\overset{―}{k} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain that 

$$
4\textrm{i}\,\overline{k}  = 8\textrm{i}-12
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\overline{k}=\dfrac{8\textrm{i}-12}{4\textrm i} = 2+3\textrm{i}.
$$

 

Therefore, $k=\overline{2+3\textrm{i}}=2-3\textrm{i}.$

Finally, $\textrm{Im}(k)=-3.$

Question 1

If x=[7−8i6] then x―=

a
[−7−8i6]
b
[−7+8i−6]
c
[7+8i6]
d
[−7−8i−6]
e

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

x―=[7−8i6]―=[7−8i―6―]=[7+8i6].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that conjugation changes 7−8i to 7+8i and leaves the real entry 6 unchanged. This matches option c; option e incorrectly changes 6 to −6.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
content.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}7-8\text{i} \\ 6\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{7-8\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{6}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+8\text{i} \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given the vectors x1=[1+i2+2i] and x2=[2−4i2+3i], then x―1+i⋅x2=

a
[5+i−1+i]
b
[−15+i]
c
[5+i−1]
d
[1−2i−5]
e
[5+i−1+4i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Conjugating x₁ gives entries 1−i and 2−2i. Multiplying x₂ by i gives 4+2i and −3+2i, since i²=−1. Adding corresponding entries gives 5+i and −1, matching option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2-4\text{i} \\ 2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ 2\text{i}+3{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4+2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5+\text{i} \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Question 2

Given the vectors x1=[1+i2+2i] and x2=[2−4i2+3i], then x―1+i⋅x2=

a
[5+i−1+i]
b
[−15+i]
c
[5+i−1]
d
[1−2i−5]
e
[5+i−1+4i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

x―1=[1+i2+2i]―=[1+i―2+2i―]=[1−i2−2i].

Multiplying the second vector, we get

i⋅x2=i⋅[2−4i2+3i]=[2i−4i22i+3i2]=[4+2i−3+2i].

Therefore, x―1+i⋅x2=[1−i2−2i]+[4+2i−3+2i]=[5+i−1].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
content.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2-4\text{i} \\ 2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ 2\text{i}+3{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4+2\text{i} \\ -3+2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5+\text{i} \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

If x=[9−6i9−3i−3] then x―=

a
[6+9i3+9i−3i]
b
[−9+6i−9+3i3]
c
[−9−6i−9−3i3]
d
[9+6i9+3i−3]
e
[6−9i3−9i−3i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Conjugation reverses the sign of each imaginary part and preserves real entries. Thus 9−6i becomes 9+6i, 9−3i becomes 9+3i, and −3 remains −3, matching option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}9-6\text{i} \\ 9-3\text{i} \\ -3\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{9-6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{9-3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9+6\text{i} \\ 9+3\text{i} \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Conjugating x₁ gives (2i, −1+4i). Multiplying x₂ by i gives (−3−i, 4−3i), using i²=−1. Adding entries gives (−3+i, 3+i), matching option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} \\ -1-4\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1-4\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1+3\text{i} \\ -3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i}+3{\text{i}}^{2} \\ -3\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Question 4

Given the vectors x1=[−2i−1−4i] and x2=[−1+3i−3−4i], then x―1+i⋅x2=

a
[1+2i4+i]
b
[4−3+i]
c
[−3+i3+i]
d
[−3−5i3−i]
e
[−1+i−3+i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

x―1=[−2i−1−4i]―=[−2i―−1−4i―]=[2i−1+4i].

Multiplying the second vector, we get

i⋅x2=i⋅[−1+3i−3−4i]=[−i+3i2−3i−4i2]=[−3−i4−3i].

Therefore, x―1+i⋅x2=[2i−1+4i]+[−3−i4−3i]=[−3+i3+i].

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
content.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} \\ -1-4\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-1-4\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1+3\text{i} \\ -3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i}+3{\text{i}}^{2} \\ -3\text{i}-4{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ -1+4\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3-\text{i} \\ 4-3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

If x=[4+3i2−2i5i] then x―=

a
[−3+4i−2+2i5]
b
[4−3i2+2i−5i]
c
[−4+3i−2−2i−5i]
d
[3−4i2+2i−5]
e
[−4−3i−2+2i−5i]
Submit

decision.explanation: Conjugation preserves real parts and reverses imaginary signs: 4+3i becomes 4−3i, 2−2i becomes 2+2i, and 5i becomes −5i. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4+3\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} \\ 5\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4+3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{5\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Vector
content.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4+3\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} \\ 5\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4+3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{5\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}c \\ d\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4+9\text{i} \\ 1+8\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $bc-ad?$
after.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4+9\text{i} \\ 1+8\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}-4+9\text{i} \\ 1+8\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $\,a=-4,b=1,c=9$ and $d=8$, which implies that 

$$
bc-ad=1\cdot 9-(-4)\cdot 8=41.
$$

Question 8
?

Find the real and imaginary parts of the vector v=[i+24−2i].

a
Re(v)=[12], Im(v)=[4−2]
b
Re(v)=[14], Im(v)=[2−2]
c
Re(v)=[21], Im(v)=[4−2]
d
Re(v)=[24], Im(v)=[1−2]
e
Re(v)=[1−2], Im(v)=[24]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since i+2=2+i, the real entries are 2 and 4, and the imaginary coefficients are 1 and −2. This matches option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Find the real and imaginary parts of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\text{i}+2 \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 \\ -\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i}+2 \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2+\text{i} \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Find the real and imaginary parts of the vector v=[i+24−2i].

a
Re(v)=[12], Im(v)=[4−2]
b
Re(v)=[14], Im(v)=[2−2]
c
Re(v)=[21], Im(v)=[4−2]
d
Re(v)=[24], Im(v)=[1−2]
e
Re(v)=[1−2], Im(v)=[24]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For the given vector v=[2i−1−i] we have that v=[i+24−2i]=[2+i4−2i]=[24]⏟Re(v)+i[1−2]⏟Im(v).

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Vector
content.problem: Find the real and imaginary parts of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\text{i}+2 \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i}-1 \\ -\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i}+2 \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2+\text{i} \\ 4-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find the real part of the vector v=[37i−4].

a
Re(v)=[0−4]
b
Re(v)=[−43]
c
Re(v)=[3−4]
d
Re(v)=[−37]
e
Re(v)=[07]
Submit

decision.explanation: The real part of 3 is 3, and the real part of 7i−4 is −4. Thus option c is correct.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Find the real part of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ -4+7\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Vector
content.problem: Find the real part of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ -4+7\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}c \\ d\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $ad+bc?$
after.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $\,a=2,b=5,c=4$ and $d=-2$, which implies that 

$$
ad+bc=2\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 4=16.
$$

decision.explanation: Since conjugation distributes over multiplication, the first entry gives 4·conjugate(k)=−20+28i. Thus conjugate(k)=−5+7i and k=−5−7i. The second entry checks: (−5+7i)(−5+i)=18−40i. Therefore Re(k)=−5.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Since $\overset{―}{kv}=\overset{―}{v},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}-20+28\text{i} \\ 18-40\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5-\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}-20+28\text{i} \\ 18-40\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4} \\ \overset{―}{-5-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-20+28\text{i} \\ 18-40\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-20+28\text{i} \\ 18-40\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\overset{―}{k} \\ (-5+\text{i})\overset{―}{k}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}4\overset{―}{k}=-20+28\text{i} \\ (-5+\text{i})\overset{―}{k}=18-40\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get

$$
\overset{―}{k}=-5+7\text{i}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain the true statement

$$
(-5+\text{i})(-5+7\text{i})=18-40\text{i}
$$

Therefore, $k=\overset{―}{-5+7\text{i}}=-5-7\text{i}.$

Finally, $\text{Re}(k)=-5.$

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Since $\overset{―}{kv}=\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}20 \\ -4+8\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4+8\text{i} \\ 4\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}20 \\ -4+8\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4+8\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}20 \\ -4+8\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}-4-8\text{i} \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}20 \\ -4+8\text{i}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-4-8\text{i})\overset{―}{k} \\ 4\overset{―}{k}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}(-4-8\text{i})\overset{―}{k}=20 \\ 4\overset{―}{k}=-4+8\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get 

$$
\overset{―}{k}=-1+2\text{i}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain the true statement

$$
(-4-8\text{i})(-1+2\text{i})=20.
$$

Therefore, $k=\overset{―}{-1+2\text{i}}=-1-2\text{i}.$

Finally, $\text{Re}(k)=-1.$
